grob.et:
From Middle High German grob, grop, from Old High German grob, girob, of uncertain origin. Compare also Low German groff, Dutch grof, Saterland Frisian groaf, and English gruff.
Per Kroonen, from Proto-West Germanic *grob, from Proto-Germanic *grubaz (“coarse”…

s: Setze mir nicht, du Grobian, / Mir den Krug so derb vor die Nase
Clown, do not clap the vessel that you bear / In such rough fashion here beneath my nose!
Grobian.et: First attested in the 15th century in the form Grobianus, shortened by the 16th century. Humorous formation from grob (“coarse”) + Latin -iānus (“-ian”). Compare Schlendrian and further Dummerjan, Liederjan (also Dummrian, Liedrian).

s: blacksmith (metalsmith who forges wrought iron or steel)
